gaps.sentence: They organized ___ charity concert for flood victims.
gaps.explanation: 'A charity concert' — one of many possible concerts, first mention.

gaps.sentence: They elected her ___ chairperson for a second term.
gaps.explanation: After 'elect/appoint', roles take no article: elected her chairperson.

gaps.sentence: She was wearing ___ old denim jacket that I loved at first sight.
gaps.explanation: 'An old…' — 'old' starts with a vowel sound.

gaps.sentence: We had ___ lunch at a bistro near the cathedral.
gaps.explanation: Names of meals (breakfast, lunch, dinner) take no article when used generally.

gaps.sentence: He's always been fascinated by ___ universe.
We had ___ wonderful time in Prague.
gaps.explanation: 'Have a wonderful/great/good time' — 'time' here is countable and takes 'a'.

gaps.sentence: She's got ___ few friends in Madrid, so she visits often.
gaps.explanation: 'A few' means some (positive); 'few' alone means hardly any.

gaps.sentence: She has ___ excellent command of Japanese.
gaps.explanation: 'Have an excellent command of' — 'excellent' starts with a vowel sound.
